key_insight: Neural networks can end up with similar final behavior while still carrying persistent internal differences from their training history.
engineering_relevance: For model development and constitutive surrogates, matching accuracy alone may hide unresolved path dependence that affects interpretability, robustness, and reuse across training protocols.
method: Paired convolutional networks started from identical weights.
They were trained in reversed task orders, then given the same deterministic common-relaxation data.
Controls tested longer relaxation, rotated MNIST, and ReLU vs. LeakyReLU activations.
evidence_signal: Across 20 paired MNIST runs, 16 met the behavioral-matching criterion, yet the mean representation-history score was 0.139 with about 3.1% prediction disagreement; the gap persisted after 50,000 updates.
watch_item: The findings are protocol-scoped, so the persistence effect may depend on dataset, optimizer, architecture, and the exact definition of representational similarity.
paper_title: Behavioral Convergence Without Representational Convergence: Persistent Training-History Dependence in Neural Networks
